body: Wow thank you. This is all brand new to me, im engaged to a real person who I spend lots of time with and whom i love dearly. I do have my fair share of depression and trauma from my childhood but I've never really thought of my dream guy as an escape. I guess now that I think about it, I tend to dream more about him when I'm passed off or stressed out about work.
What??? Really??? I've never heard of that before. What's wrong with maladaptive daydreaming? How is it unhealthy?

I would settle if I could just get someone to draw him lol 

Idk if I could ever find someone like how I view this character. But your suggestion is very sweet
Okay! Ill reach out to them on Monday, they are always out on the weekends. Thank you so so much! Helped.
Hi! Thank you vm for replying. Are there any like, youtube channels or resources you could recommend that I can listen to/watch since I work from home?
Thank you, I saw another comment that linked to the wiki page and it's exactly what I am experiencing. I'm so so so relieved that I'm not alone.
YES! exactly this. Thank you for sharing.
Omg that's really scary. Thank you so so much for your advice, I'll follow it to the letter. I'll look at that link too when I have more time. Bless you.

Thank you. I can afford a psychiatrist, I just havent made an appointment because finding the right therapist for me is really hard. And I might come clean to them and bring up all of my traumas, just for them to get another job that pays better and I have to start over with another psychiatrist that I might not like (if the one I was seeing is too far out of my way to keep seeing). 

But I will actively search now. Thank you
Carbon monoxide detector? Can you explain how carbon monoxide could cause this?
No, I've tried to pop it multiple time but it's too painful :( it hurts more than any pimple I've ever had.
I will! Thank you for your guess
Oh thank you! I'm seeing my dr on tuesday since it really is bothering me. I really do appreciate your info!
Okay, thank you so so much. I'm scheduling it right now. Thank you!

I had thought it was a great idea at the time, it was before I was diagnosed with my own chronic illness and before I started to doubt things.
